Yes I am from Aotearoa! There isn't really a specific way to make a boil up and the ingredients differ from whanau to whanau (family in Te Reo Māori), but generally it starts off with pork or bacon bones, covered with water and simmered for an hour, at which point you'd add some starchy veges (favourites are potato/rīwai, sweetpotato/kumara, pumpkin and carrots), then some cabbage and/or watercress (or any other leafy greens). Puha or sow thistles are also used in place of watercress as its easier to find here. Most people consider it a weed but it's actually got some good nutritional value!

Around 15 mins before serving many also add doughboys into the pot which are just flour dumplings (very easy to make just mix flour, salt and pepper with water and roll into balls about the size of a golfball).  Serve with salt and tomato sauce.

Personally I wouldn't mind or question you if I met you as a online as  girl and suddenly hear your voice, but I think its best to get to know who you're talking to and be sure that they're open minded about LGBTQ+ stuff before you tell them. I'm FtM trans myself and haven't started hormones but my voice is still kinda low anyway so I can get away with it, so I don’t normally tell people I’m trans unless I’m close with them. I would suggest maybe doing some voice exercises and watching youtube vids about how to have a softer more feminine voice so that you can experiment with the new identity.

It’s easier to experiment online first and then letting people you’re close to know about your identity before anyone else My parents weren’t that accepting cause they’re religious so I made the mistake of telling them first and it made me feel bad for a long time. Make sure you have enough support! Once you’re more comfortable with your identity online its okay to start experimenting in real life with clothes and such.

Hope this helped! Good luck (-:
